keyFindings.description: ARCHITECT'S SETTLED DECISION of 2026-10-21 04:22Z, carried into this round as the architect's and not as a finding of the reviewer's: now that the guard exists, delete the mirrored `const dispatchServerStopGrace = 30` (:531), TestDispatchAppPodGracePeriodCoversThePreStopWaitAndTheServersShutdown (:539) and `toInt` (:559, no other caller in the module). Its reason, in the architect's words: a hand-copy of a number that lives in another module and that nothing checks reads as a guarantee and goes stale silently, so keeping it beside the real guard leaves two claims about one relation with the decorative one in the place an infra editor meets first. This did not land in round 3 because it was lost in transit, not declined: the implementer's process died around 04:22Z, its workspace was recreated, the task it was re-sent carried round 1's text, and the only durable copy it could read was this handoff's round-2 keyFindings, where the item stood as the reviewer's batched maintainability minor because that is what it was before the architect overrode it. The implementer has since agreed and spelled the deletion line for line. It is not a pure deletion and all of it lands together: :519, inside the test that is kept, reads the constant, so the module stops compiling unless that assertion spells its own 5 and 35; :511-512 points the reader at the test being deleted; and pod_grace_period_test.go:45-46 ("that module's own test mirrors stopGrace by hand") becomes stale by design. The golden pin and TestDispatchAppPodKeepsServingUntilItsRemovalFromRoutingPropagates stay: they answer for the rendered pod whatever the server does.

The comment that justifies the pre-stop hook states the Kubernetes ordering backwards, and so does its copy at dispatch_test.go:505-507. Both say the EndpointSlice controller, every node's proxy and Tailscale Serve learn of a terminating pod only after the kubelet has sent it SIGTERM. The control plane removes the pod from its EndpointSlice when the deletionTimestamp appears, concurrently with the kubelet starting termination — the hook first, SIGTERM on its return — and that concurrency is the whole reason a pre-stop sleep helps. Under the comment's model propagation begins when the sleep has already ended, so the wait would buy nothing, and the sentence contradicts its own next clause. README.md:209-211, rewritten in this same round, states the correct model, so the pull request now ships two texts that disagree on the point round 2 asked to be made honest. The reviewer's own round-2 review body asserted that the code comment had it right and the README did not; that was wrong, and this review says so on the record rather than leaving it standing. It matters because INFRA-63 retunes exactly this five seconds, and under the wrong model the number is unrelated to the window it is sized for.

The two backlinks added in round 3 over-promise what the guard catches: "pod_grace_period_test.go fails when the two drift" (shutdown.go:19, and the same clause at packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:173). The guard asserts grace - wait >= stopGrace, so it catches the pod falling short and says nothing about the pod's grace being raised alone. That is the right asymmetry — only one direction is dangerous — but the claim as written is not what the code does, which is the class of defect this review has blocked on twice. "fails when the pod's budget stops covering it" is the true claim.

`needed := int(stopGrace / time.Second)` truncates, so a sub-second raise of stopGrace is the one edit the guard does not catch: at stopGrace = 30s500ms, needed is 30 and 35 - 5 = 30 passes while the pod is 500 ms short. Every whole-second raise is caught. Two lines close it: compare durations, `time.Duration(grace-wait)*time.Second < stopGrace`, and format stopGrace in the message. Asked for in the same push because it is the guard's own soundness, not a separate concern.

declined.reason: Declined, not overlooked, and recorded so the next reader sees it was weighed. Its evidence is right — packages/envoy/infra/go.mod replaces github.com/sjawhar/envoy with ../, gcp/dispatch.go imports internal/bus from production code, and core/listener_env.go:20 already derives a constant across that boundary — and the reviewer put exactly that legality to the architect at round 2, so the choice was made in full knowledge of it. The architect chose the guard: an exported constant makes the infra module's import of the server's internals a supported surface for the sake of one integer, and whoever changes the number is in package main either way, which is where the guard fires. The decision stands. Its if-declined requirement about the stale doc comment is folded into the first finding above.

thermonuclear.deepReview: No blocking correctness or security defect. It confirmed the delta is test-and-docs only — no rendered object and no runtime path changes, and shutdown.go's hunk is comment-only with the constant untouched — and that the guard bites in every case asked and fails rather than skips: stopGrace raised, the pod's grace lowered, the sleep raised, the hook dropped, the container renamed, the golden moved, its shape changed. Two minors, both carried into this review: the backwards ordering comment and the truncation at :89.
thermonuclear.codeQuality: One finding it called blocking, declined above with its reason. Its F2 is carried into this review's first finding: the settled deletion breaks a compile at dispatch_test.go:519 and dangles two pointers, so all of it lands together. Fast-follows recorded, not asked for now: roughly forty of the guard's ninety-four lines are shape ceremony for a one-line inequality (four levels of pointer-to-anonymous-struct, a found flag, two constants naming one file, a 457-character failure message); the rollout paragraph in the infra README is twenty-four lines and six subjects long, and the causal chain at :215-217 is dispatch_kube.go:299-301 almost verbatim; and both round-3 inserts left an unfinished rewrap. It checked the earlier fast-follows and found none worse, no Go file past a thousand lines, and no copy-paste in the three-Deployment split.
